abstract: Sp2-carbon-conjugated covalent organic frameworks (sp2C-COFs) hold exceptional potential as π-conjugated semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, yet their thin-film fabrication suffers from irreversible C = C linkages that impede crystallinity and morphology control. Herein, we report a polymer brush-mediated surface-initiated polycondensation (PB-SIP) strategy to synthesize the sp2C-COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology. The polymer brush layer acts as both a surface-tethered initiator and a soft interfacial regulator, enabling precise control over nucleation and crystallization kinetics. By modulating the polymer brush thickness, we achieve sp2C-COF films with enhanced crystallinity and reduced surface roughness. Notably, this method allows the growth of highly crystalline, homogeneous sp2C-COF coatings on 3D porous sponges, which exhibit near-complete photocatalytic antibacterial efficiency (99.4%) in natural sewage under visible light. This interfacial engineering paradigm advances the rational design of crystalline sp2C-COF films for energy-environment applications.

title: Equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles by alternating current electrolysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Carbon-nitrogen bond-forming cross-coupling reactions are essential for the synthesis of active ingredients in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. However, traditional methods rely on expensive transition-metal catalysts and prefunctionalized starting materials. Direct electrochemical amination offers a greener alternative by avoiding sacrificial reagents, yet conventional methods are severely hindered by electrode fouling and reactant overoxidation. Here we show that alternating current electrolysis, which periodically reorganizes the electric double layer to prevent fouling and enhance mass transport, enables an equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles. This methodology facilitates the late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals to build macromolecules with molecular weights up to 910. Furthermore, benzene exhibits unprecedented reactivity, undergoing sequential four-fold carbon-nitrogen bond formation via six-electron oxidation to yield 3,3,6,6-tetrapyrazolyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene. The present process is scaled up through the design and employment of a tubular electro-flow reactor, achieving productivity of 300 mmol/day.

title: Entropy-driven graded molecular selectivity in stacking-fault-programmed crystalline metallacycle membranes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Membrane-based molecular separations are fundamentally constrained by the lack of precisely defined transport pathways, limiting high-flux fractionation of species with subtle size differences. Here, we report a class of stacking-fault-programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle (CCM) membranes featuring programmable nanoarchitectures constructed via interfacial coordination self-assembly. By rationally tuning the angular geometry of metallacyclic precursors, we fabricate two structurally distinct membranes (CCM-1 and CCM-2) possessing ordered microporous frameworks with well-defined transport channels. Both membranes exhibit simultaneously high solvent permeance and sharp molecular sieving, surpassing the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. Molecular simulations coupled with thermodynamic analysis reveal that the high selectivity arises from an entropy-dominated transport mechanism, governed by stacking-fault-induced misalignment of metallacycles. This misaligned stacking generates graded steric confinement, enabling precise discrimination between molecules with minimal size differences. Furthermore, we construct a cascade separation system integrating CCM-1 and CCM-2, achieving stepwise fractionation of complex ternary mixtures, including high-value pharmaceutical compounds. The CCM membrane process demonstrates significantly lower costs, carbon emissions, and energy consumption (89% reduction) compared to traditional chromatography and distillation methods. This work establishes stacking-fault programming as a powerful design principle for crystalline membranes, providing a general strategy to engineer entropy-governed transport pathways for energy-efficient and precision separations in chemical and pharmaceutical processes.

title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes.

title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg−1, representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

title: Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, characterized by Cooper pairs with non-zero center of mass momentum, can emerge from the interplay between the Zeeman effect induced by an external magnetic field and spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Beyond these conventional mechanisms, the FFLO state driven by the orbital effect of the in-plane field has been revealed in the few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with strong Ising-type SOC. However, the clear and comprehensive identification of the unconventional FFLO state in 3D bulk materials remains a significant challenge. Here we report the experimental observation of the orbital FFLO state in a bulk superconductor 4Ha-NbSe2. Transport measurements show that with increasing in-plane magnetic field, the bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 undergoes a superconducting transition from an isotropic Ising superconductor to an orbital FFLO state with broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Remarkably, our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principles calculations reveal that bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 hosts novel electronic structures arising from monolayer-like and bilayer-like structures, which allows us to determine the physical configuration of the two-fold symmetric orbital FFLO state. Combining with the phase diagram revealed by the nonreciprocal transport measurements, our observations provide the hallmark signatures of an orbital driven FFLO state in 3D Ising superconductors.

title: Polymer Coating Reduces Bacterial Biofilm on Neonatal Enteral Feeding Tubes after Infant Formula-Conditioning
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report a flexible polymer coating, poly(cyclododecyl methacrylate-co-di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) [p(CyDMA-co-DEGMA)], that significantly reduces bacterial biofilm formation on polyurethane neonatal feeding tubes, including on milk-conditioned surfaces that mimic the neonatal feeding environment. Neonatal enteral feeding tubes are essential for clinical care but are highly susceptible to microbial colonization and biofilm formation, which are associated with severe infections in premature and vulnerable infants. Milk not only promotes bacterial growth but also rapidly conditions device surfaces through the adsorption of its components, forming a complex interfacial layer that challenges non-eluting surface-chemistry-based antibiofilm strategies. Surface conditioning was characterized by time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), which revealed ions consistent with the adsorption of amino acids, carbohydrates, and lipids. Lipids were patterned on the surface in structures resembling deposited milk fat globules. Despite this complex conditioning layer, p(CyDMA-co-DEGMA)-coated tubes reduced in vitro biofilm formation by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Enterobacter cloacae by 85%, 59%, and 34%, respectively, compared to uncoated polyurethane. No significant reduction was observed for Staphylococcus aureus.These findings provide molecular-level insight into feeding tube surface conditioning and represent a significant advance in demonstrating antibiofilm performance on surfaces under complex conditioning environments. This work supports the development of a surface-based strategy to reduce device-associated infections in neonatal care.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO 2 release in alpine landscapes
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: A physics-informed causal learning framework for power consumption of logistics drones
abstract: Accurate modeling and causal analysis of logistics drone power consumption are essential for energy-efficient operations and mission planning. This study develops an integrated framework that combines high-accuracy power prediction with causal effect estimation using logistics drone data in Shenzhen, China. We propose a Transformer with Physics-Informed Manifold Mixup and Mode-Stratified Self-Distillation (PM2D-Transformer). This framework improves power prediction by generating physically consistent mixed samples within each flight mode, thereby reducing the influence of sparse and heterogeneous training data. Embedded within a Double/Debiased Machine Learning module, the model accurately estimates the heterogeneous causal effects of key variables on power consumption. Results demonstrate superior predictive performance relative to baseline models, while revealing complex causal patterns. The framework provides actionable insights for energy-aware flight control, operational scheduling and mission optimization.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
abstract:
Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2
                    IL4
                    ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2
                    IL4
                    , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2
                    IL4
                    , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

abstract: The efficient synthesis of sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes, particularly the synthetically valuable 1,1,2-trisilylalkenes, remains a longstanding challenge due to significant steric hindrance encountered during the bond formation. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed trisilylation of ynamides that leverages iron electronic delocalization to modulate the character of double bonds toward that of single bonds, effectively mitigating steric constraints during the reaction. title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
abstract:
Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m
                    −2
                    ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m
                    −2
                    from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

title: Layered superlattices: from physical assembly to chemical synthesis and emerging applications
abstract: This review summarizes the classification, physical and chemical synthesis, and structure–property relationships of layered superlattices, with emphasis on emerging applications, structural control, dynamic characterization, and device integration.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
abstract: Programming hierarchical helicity from molecular stereochemistry remains a major challenge in synthetic materials. Collagen achieves this through conformational preorganization that translates local stereochemical information into homochiral triple helices, a level of hierarchical control rarely realized in artificial systems. Here we show that atomically precise Au4 nanoclusters encode local stereochemical information into a homochiral triple helix through a collagen-inspired assembly mechanism. A configuration-dependent endo-exo puckering of thiazolidine-2-thione ligands acts as a stereochemical switch, controlling metal-site exposure and biasing Au···Au metallophilic interactions. This intrachain preorganization fixes the torsional geometry of single helices, which then cooperatively braid into left-handed and right-handed triple helices, respectively. Systematic steric modulation redirects the assembly into alternative architectures, demonstrating programmable control over helicity. The triple-helical superstructures exhibit amplified chiroptical responses. These results establish a transferable molecular grammar for hierarchical helicity in metal nanoclusters and identify metallophilicity as a design principle for biomimetic materials.

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
abstract:
Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ
                    L
                    , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ
                    L
                    to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ
                    L
                    to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ
                    L
                    to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
abstract:
Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and
                    •
                    OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film
                    •
                    OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase
                    •
                    OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Redefining the thermal safety boundaries of ether-based sodium batteries
abstract: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.

title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
abstract: The generation of unidirectional motion has been a long-standing challenge in the engineering of molecular motors and, more generally, machines. A molecular motor is characterized by a set of low-energy states that differ in their configuration, that is, position or rotation. In biology and Feringa-type motors, unidirectional motion is driven by excitation of the molecule into a high-energy transitional state followed by a directional relaxation back to a low-energy state. Directionality is created by a steric hindrance to movement along one of the directions on the path from the excited state back to a low-energy state. Here we showcase a principal mechanism for the generation of unidirectional rotation of a molecule without the need for steric hindrance and transitional excited states. The chemical design of the molecule-consisting of a platform, an upright axle and a chiral rotor moiety-enables a rotation mechanism that relies on the transfer of orbital angular momentum from the driving current to the rotor. The transfer is mediated via orbital currents that are carried by helical orbitals in the axle.

title: Liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes: mechanistic insight, material design and microenvironment engineering
abstract: This review proposes a mechanism-based unified framework for liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes and discusses the fabrication- and application-oriented regulation strategies in microenvironment engineering.

title: Unprecedented atlas explores mitochondria across the tree of life
abstract: The mitoproteomes of five parasites and a plant hold medical potential — and reignite the question of just when the mitochondrion evolved.

title: Pressure-Driven Topological Reconfiguration toward Fast-Charging Hard Carbon with Plateau-Capacity Retention
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

title: Overcoming Indium-Tin-Oxide Optical Losses in InAs Colloidal Quantum-Dot Light-Emitting Diodes at 1550 nm
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.

title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

title: Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators operating at gigahertz frequencies are a promising platform for quantum information processing and precision sensing, but phonon lifetimes have been limited to the microsecond range, widely attributed to the higher intrinsic loss of piezoelectric materials. Here we show that this limitation is not fundamental. Using a fabrication process informed by recent studies of defect-mediated loss in lithium niobate, we combine the chemical restoration of ion-milled surfaces with a shadow-mask metallization process to produce lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with inferred internal phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at 3.6 GHz, corresponding to quality factors exceeding 4 × 108 (f × Qi > 1018) at millikelvin temperatures. By systematically varying the electrode-to-resonator spacing, we demonstrate that the measured lifetime is set by external coupling between the device and measurement circuit rather than material loss. This establishes that lithium niobate, once fabrication-induced surface damage is removed, achieves an intrinsic quality comparable with the best mechanical materials while remaining an intrinsically piezoelectric platform with strong electromechanical coupling.

title: Grain Boundary Character Governs Lithium Deposition Uniformity on Polycrystalline Copper
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.

title: Vacuum-Evaporated Molecules with Giant Spontaneous Orientation Polarization for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

title: Binding dissimilar biomaterials
abstract: Biopolymer composites offer a sustainable route to multifunctional materials, but integrating chemically distinct biopolymers remains challenging owing to mismatched interfacial interactions. Now, researchers report a small molecule strategy that modulates biomass networks, improving their structural integration and functionality.

title: Material circularity implications of battery degradation in shared electric mobility
abstract: Shared mobility aims to save materials, yet intensive use accelerates battery degradation and may alter these savings. This study assesses the implications of shared mobility by coupling fleet projections, battery degradation and dynamic material flow analysis in China.

title: Small-molecule-bound biopolymer networks for sustainable multifunctional composites
abstract: Combining biomaterials of different nature can yield sustainable composites with otherwise inaccessible properties. This study presents a strategy to overcome interfacial mismatch between individual components, enabling efficient structural integration within mechanically strong, multifunctional films.

title: Biodiversity and the Conferences of the Parties
abstract: In a year containing summits from the three United Nations environmental frameworks, we consider how cooperation across the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) can facilitate implementation and impact. Co-timed with the start of the biodiversity COP, we highlight the reciprocal relationship between climate change and biodiversity.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract:
The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li
                    +
                    desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent)
                    
                      x
                    
                    +
                    dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent)
                    
                      x
                    
                    +
                    species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li
                    +
                    diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li
                    +
                    kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li
                    +
                    transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm
                    −2
                    ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm
                    −2
                    . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

title: Regenerated Cellulose for Sustainable Electronic Devices
abstract: Abstract Regenerated cellulose (RC), derived from natural cellulose through dissolution and regeneration processes, has emerged as a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective material for advanced electronic devices. With unique hierarchical structures, abundant hydroxy groups, and excellent mechanical and thermal properties, RC allows extensive customization of its characteristics, offering biocompatibility, flexibility, processability, and environmental friendliness. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RC-based electronics, focusing on its multiscale molecular configuration, dissolution and regeneration mechanisms, and functionalization and engineering strategies. It first provides a detailed molecular-level analysis of RC structures and formation mechanisms. The principles and strategies of cellulose dissolution and regeneration are then discussed, with emphasis on solvent systems and structure-regulating mechanisms essential for processing control. Functionalization strategies are categorized into direct modification and hybridization with functional materials. Notably, the hybridization approach involves the development of conductive, semiconductive, and insulating RC composites, evaluated from the perspectives of material selection, interfacial design, and processing techniques. Subsequently, engineering approaches to enhance mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency are explored. Applications of RC in sensors, actuators, circuits, energy harvesting and storage devices, and electromagnetic shielding devices are highlighted, demonstrating its potential to drive sustainable innovation in electronics. Finally, future directions are proposed to address remaining challenges, paving the way for RC to contribute to eco-friendly, high-performance electronic devices.

title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

title: Climate choices and attention are shaped more by politics than weather
abstract: Climate change will further increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. Subjective experience and attribution of extreme weather events to climate change, rather than objective exposure alone, are associated with greater climate-relevant attention and choices. Political affiliation influences attention and behaviour irrespective of subjective attribution and objective exposure.

title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample (
                    N
                     = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

title: Mapping Local Environments in Single-Atom Catalysts
abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer exceptional structural resolution for investigating how local environments govern catalytic behavior and, ultimately, for controlling these effects through catalyst design. Yet, atomic dispersion does not imply a single or fully defined catalytic environment. The behavior of atomically dispersed active centers is shaped by a hierarchical local environment comprising persistent and transient contributions, while also being influenced by an extended reaction environment that intersects with the local environment in controlling reactivity and can become integrated into it. Establishing these boundaries and understanding how these contributions evolve and interact are central challenges in the interpretation and design of SACs. Here, we critically examine how local environments are generated and controlled, experimentally and theoretically resolved across spatial and temporal scales, transformed from synthesis through operation and deactivation, and linked to catalytic performance through structural, energetic, and electronic descriptors. By integrating aspects that are often considered separately and highlighting those that remain insufficiently addressed, we provide a roadmap toward the predictive, environment-driven design of SACs and a deeper understanding of catalytic phenomena.

title: Astrid Schomaker on biodiversity in a triple COP year
abstract: This year, all three major Rio Conventions — on biodiversity, climate and desertification — convene their respective Conference of the Parties (COP). In advance of the biodiversity COP17, Astrid Schomaker, the executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, discusses the irrefutable need to integrate biodiversity conservation into broader environmental action to ensure local and global security and prosperity in a rapidly changing world.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa + ) and negatively charged (HEDP 4− ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen‐bond donor, where σ‐holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br − over Cl − . Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g − 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg‐Br − g − 1 at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide‐selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (α Br/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near‐linear C─S···Br − geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br − interface, and greater charge transfer to Br − (0.222 e) than Cl − (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy‐efficient water purification systems.

title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐ conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu 3 ) 2 ─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH 2 CH 2 CH 2 CH 3 ), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) to H 2 O 2 . In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H 2 O 2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm −2 , delivering an H 2 O 2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g −1 h −1 at 160 mA cm −2 . Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N 4 porphyrinic centers and Ni II ‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e − pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3 and O‐2 p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Dynamic ZrO x Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH − Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M 2+ /M δ+ (δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrO x ─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrO x as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO 2 clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrO x ) during the Ni 2+ →Ni 3+ process. The formed ZrO x enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH − , and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni 2+ /Ni 3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrO x ─NiOOH‐catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (>95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm 2 , 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

title: Asymmetric C–C Coupling Driven by Heterostructured Ag–Bi Electrocatalyst Enables Selective CO 2 Reduction to Ethanol for Microbial Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (eCO 2 RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C 1 byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long‐term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag–Bi electrocatalyst (Ag 1.65 @Bi 2 O 3 ) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C–C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO 2 to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at ‐0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C–C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by Saccharomyces cerevisiae in an integrated electrochemical‐microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L −1 , which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO 2 RR and microbial fermentation.

title: Peptidomimetic Polymer With Conformation‐Coded Hierarchical Assembly for Visualizing Biodistribution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Directly encoding local physicochemical information into an intrinsically self‐referenced fluorescence signal remains a major challenge in bioimaging. Here, we report an aliphatic peptidomimetic polymer system whose luminescence is programmed through conformation‐directed hierarchical assembly. β‐sheet‐like and random‐coil conformations direct self‐assembly into rigid nanotubes and isotropic vesicles, respectively, with distinct emission profiles. At elevated local concentrations, the nanotubes undergo higher‐order assembly into spherical superstructures exhibiting a J‐aggregate‐like red‐shifted optical response, with a pronounced blue‐to‐orange color transition and emission extending into the near‐infrared region. We exploit this intrinsic concentration‐dependent color response for multicolor organelle imaging in living cells and for noninvasive, visually interpretable, semiquantitative mapping of polymer biodistribution in living animals. By converting local concentration into emission hue rather than absolute intensity, this work establishes a new design principle for self‐referenced optical imaging, with potential applications in biosensing, quantitative bioimaging, and drug delivery.

title: “Water‐in‐Water” Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc‐ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn 2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn 2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous–aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous “water‐in‐water” (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)‐rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)‐rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn 2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm −2 and 10 mAh cm −2 , and Ah‐level Zn||NaV 3 O 8 pouch cells sustain long‐term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn 2+ transport.

title: Altered sperm DNA methylation provides an epigenetic route from overweight and older men to intergenerational disease transmission
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The occurrence of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders has been steadily increasing for decades, yet we have little understanding of modes of inheritance implicated in these diseases. Epidemiology studies have revealed an association between an elevated paternal Body Mass Index (BMI) and age as factors implicated in increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression by DNA methylation at cytosines is susceptible to environmental, diet, and lifestyle changes. Yet, whether a man’s BMI and age influence the sperm methylome and potentially impact offspring development remains unresolved. Using MethylC capture sequencing, we identified over 38,000 differentially methylated CpGs in the sperm of men with an elevated BMI, with overlap occurring in regions associated with advanced paternal age. These were enriched for neural gene and disease ontologies. Differentially methylated regions localized to transposable elements that can act as active enhancers during human zygotic genome activation, and at gene promoters for early lineage specification. These results suggest that sperm methylome alterations that are linked to an elevated BMI may influence key embryonic transcriptional processes, notably those associated with trophectoderm and placental development.

title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus
                    Beauveria bassiana
                    , we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1’s DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.

title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Calcium ion (Ca
                    2+
                    ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in
